thought.text: I accidentally deleted the WAR files (not just the exploded dirs) with the cleanup glob. Re-copying and restarting:

reasoning_content:
Hmm — "Server startup in [3646] milliseconds" — that's way too fast. And the deployDirectory host-manager completed, but there's no mention of WAR deployment? Wait — the WARs have been deleted… I ran `rm -rf /opt/tomcat-api/webapps/xplan-*` — that deleted the directories, but the .war files were… let me check: `rm -rf /opt/tomcat-api/webapps/xplan-*` deletes both the directories and the .war files! The earlier cleanup commands also used the same glob — but back then, the WARs were still there because… no wait, in the previous cleanup I also used `for w in /opt/tomcat-$t/webapps/xplan-*; do [ -d "$w" ] && rm -rf "$w"; done` with a `[ -d ]` check, so only the directories got deleted. This time I used `rm -rf /opt/tomcat-api/webapps/xplan-*` without the directory check — which means I also deleted the .war files!

I need to re-copy the API's WARs.

action.command:
ls /opt/tomcat-api/webapps/; cp /tmp/dist/web/xplan-manager-api.war /tmp/dist/web/xplan-validator-api.war /tmp/dist/web/xplan-dokumente-api.war /opt/tomcat-api/webapps/
unset CATALINA_PID; /opt/tomcat-api/bin/shutdown.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 8
for p in $(ps aux | grep "[c]atalina.base=/opt/tomcat-api" | awk '{print $2}'); do kill "$p" 2>/dev/null; done; sleep 4
source /etc/xplanbox.env
CATALINA_PID=/opt/tomcat-api/tomcat.pid /opt/tomcat-api/bin/startup.sh; echo "restarted $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
